objectives: Hear /s/ followed immediately by /n/ at the beginning of taught words.
Blend /s/ and /n/ smoothly without inserting an extra vowel.
Distinguish the sn onset from /s/ alone and other taught blends.
Blend the onset with the remaining sounds and say the complete word.
concepts: Both consonants remain audible and in order.
No extra vowel belongs between the onset consonants.

definitions.definition: Two consonant sounds heard together at the start of a word.
A speech sound that can distinguish one word from another.
Joining speech sounds in order to say a word.

workedExamples.solution: Hear /s/ then /n/, followed by the rest of the word.
Snap begins with sn; sun begins with /s/ alone.
Keep /s/ and /n/ in order, then blend the rest.

commonMistakes: Dropping /n/ and saying sap for snap.
Guessing before hearing the whole word.
keyTakeaways: Do not insert an extra vowel.
Blend the onset with the rest of the word.
revisionPoints: Snap and snip begin with sn.
Listen to the whole word before choosing.
